title: Sending your work to the server

terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the server and your copy of it, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Send gift-vouchers to the server
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. Wilma has read your voucher fix and says yes. Your `gift-vouchers` has the fix and the merge with her link, and the server's `gift-vouchers` has neither yet.

Send your `gift-vouchers` to the server's `gift-vouchers`.

The check expects the server's `gift-vouchers` to have your fix and Wilma's link.
nextSteps: Switch to `gift-vouchers` and run `git status`: ahead of origin/gift-vouchers by 2 commits.
Send it with the command from the lesson.
Read what Git prints: the old and new commit, and `gift-vouchers -> gift-vouchers`.
Run `git status` again: up to date with origin/gift-vouchers.
hints: Sending commits to a remote is a push. It goes the other way from a fetch.
With no names, a push sends the branch you are on to the server branch it follows, so be on gift-vouchers.

tasks.title: Commit the August closing on main
tasks.description:
Wilma closes the shop for a week to count the stock. On `main`, open `shop/visit.html` and add this line just under the phone number: ```

Closed for stocktaking from 10 to 16 August.

``` Save it and commit it on `main`. Change no other file. Then you can try to send `main` to the server, and read what Git says. The check expects a commit on `main` whose `visit.html` has that line, with every other line as it was.
nextSteps: Switch to `main`; `git status` says up to date with origin/main, as of the last fetch.
Add the line in the editor, save, stage and commit.
Push `main` and read the message: rejected, and why.
Leave it there for now: the next task deals with it.
hints: The closing week goes on main, the site, not on gift-vouchers.
Copy the line from the task into visit.html under the phone number, then stage and commit as always.
On main, add the line and save, then run `git add visit.html` and `git commit -m "Say the shop is closed from 10 to 16 August"`.

tasks.title: Bring Femi's newest find into main
tasks.description:
This morning Femi sent one more find to the server, so the server's `main` has a commit yours does not, and Git refused your push. Bring Femi's commit into your `main`, next to your closing week. Git joins the two with a merge commit, and you can keep the message it writes.

The check expects your `main` to have Femi's newest find, and no merge left open.
nextSteps: On `main`, read the push message again: the server has work you do not have.
Pull, keeping Git's message for the merge commit without an editor.
Run `git log --oneline --graph`: your commit and Femi's meet in a merge commit.
Run `git status`: ahead of origin/main, and no longer behind.
hints: A push is only taken when it moves the server's branch forward. Yours would drop Femi's commit, so it was refused.
Pull on main, as in the last issue. Both sides have a commit, so the merge makes a merge commit.

tasks.title: Send main to the server again
tasks.description:
Now your `main` has everything the server's has, and your closing week on top. Send it to the server again.

The check expects the server's `main` to have your closing week and Femi's newest find.
nextSteps: Make sure you are on `main` and `git status` says ahead of origin/main.
Read what Git prints: this time the old and new commit, with no rejected.
Run `git status`: up to date with origin/main.
hints: Since the pull, your main has Femi's commit, so the push moves the server's main forward.
The same push as before, on main, now goes through.
